notes: Independent strategy_lab.db; the trading bot database is never read or written.
Telegram events are mirrored from the existing channel_monitor through a fire-and-forget localhost hook.
MEXC prices are consumed from the existing WebSocket IPC as a read-only client.
ENTRY without numeric Entry1 is treated as market-ready and enters on the first live price after the signal.
DCA variants use 75 USDT Entry1 and 25 USDT Entry2 only when the signal contains Entry2.
DCA TARGETS variants continue to channel targets after Entry2; split variants preserve 50/30/20 or 40/30/20/10 reservations.
FIXED TP/SL tests all 12 combinations: targets 1-4% crossed with stops 1-3%, measured from actual Entry1.
FIXED RR grids test stop distances 0.1-1.0% with target multipliers ×10 and ×15 from actual Entry1.
POST-STOP strategy doubles Entry1 from 75 to 150 USDT only on the next same-channel/same-symbol signal after its preceding losing stop.
Signals for the same symbol from different channels within 60 minutes are linked, ordered and compared without merging their results.
Cross-channel ranks count distinct channels only; exact same-channel reposts within five minutes are excluded from pattern analysis.
The dashboard channel filter uses full-history per-channel aggregates, including POST-STOP double-entry results.
Capital capacity is calculated separately for every channel + strategy pair; recommended capital adds a 10% buffer to historical peak committed capital.
Every OPEN variant closes at market after exactly 24h from Entry1; every WAITING signal expires after 24h.
Market-ready symbols without a MEXC price are ignored after 15 minutes.
Price ticks are coalesced per symbol and exchange symbols without active Lab rows are ignored.
Existing database rows remain unchanged; newly added strategies begin with signals received after this upgrade.
Each strategy has a reporting-only virtual balance of 1000000000 USDT; capital never rejects an eligible signal.
DCA trailing resets its peak after Entry2 and arms only after weighted-average recovery is reached.
GitHub publication is a separate background task; failures never stop simulation or the trading bot.
